note: The second core fit in this batch and, on the stated criteria, an even cleaner one than Ken Dunham. He owns his own business — an interior design studio he built after leaving tech, now two and a half years in with an assistant handling back office — which is the 'they own their own business' clause almost literally. Income is evidenced rather than asserted: a funded surrogacy in Colombia, a purpose-built garage gym, DEXA scans every six weeks, an existing paid coaching subscription, annual Burning Man, and a husband who is a tech marketing executive. He described the price as a latte and a croissant a day. Health is the neglected corner of an otherwise well-run life and nothing about it is a crisis — 163 lb at 5'9.5" and roughly 16% body fat, three sessions a week, rating his own physique a seven out of ten and wanting 10-12%. That is good-to-great stated in the prospect's own numbers. He is the opposite of deconditioned. Worth flagging for the rollup: both core-fit prospects in this batch are men in their forties and sixties who arrived pre-sold on Trevor, and the two things that stopped or nearly stopped them buying were operational — payment mechanics and closing steps — not price.
